final_message:
I reproduced the bug on this checkout (4f08332, ESLint 9.14.0), so it is still present after v9.4.0. I ran it on Linux and simulated Windows path behavior; I didn't run it on a real Windows machine.

**Run:** `node -r ./repro/simulate-windows.js repro/repro.js` (exits 1 when the bug shows up)

- `repro/simulate-windows.js` is a preload. It makes every `require("path")` / `require("node:path")` return `path.win32`, and it makes `process.cwd()` return `C:\Project`.
- `repro/repro.js` checks two files with `Linter#verify` and `ESLint#lintText`, using a config with only `no-undef: error` and no config lookup. Both files are outside the base path: `C:\Other\foo.js` (same drive, the control) and `F:\foo.js` (other drive). `lintText` uses the same `getConfigStatus` check as the CLI path in the report.

**Output:**
```
path.relative(cwd, C:\Other\foo.js) = "..\\Other\\foo.js"
path.relative(cwd, F:\foo.js)        = "F:\\foo.js"
[Linter] C:\Other\foo.js: IGNORED  -> "No matching configuration found for C:\Other\foo.js."
[Linter] F:\foo.js:        LINTED   -> no-undef "'foo' is not defined."
[ESLint] C:\Other\foo.js: IGNORED  -> "File ignored because outside of base path."
[ESLint] F:\foo.js:        LINTED   -> no-undef "'foo' is not defined."
BUG REPRODUCED
```

**Likely cause:** `@eslint/config-array` 0.18.0, in `ConfigArray#getConfigWithStatus` (`node_modules/@eslint/config-array/dist/cjs/index.cjs` ~L953), decides a file is outside the base path only if `path.relative(this.basePath, filePath).startsWith("..")`. On Windows, when the two paths are on different drives, `path.relative` returns the target's absolute path (`F:\foo.js`) instead of a `..` path. The check misses it, so the file is linted with the base config.

The same `startsWith("..")` pattern appears in `isDirectoryIgnored` (~L1178) and `shouldIgnorePath` (~L502). Both `Linter` (`lib/linter/linter.js` L1524 creates `FlatConfigArray` with `basePath: cwd`) and `ESLint` go through this code.

I haven't changed any ESLint source; the only additions are the two files under `repro/`.
